      "observations": [
        "All 16 owned paths and all 1,138 normal-diff lines were read. The patch adds the default-false extensions.experiments.suppressed preference and a comma-separated allowed-ID preference. parseManifest loads each add-on manifest and suppresses only an Experiment when the pref is true, its ID is not allowed and it is not temporarily installed. The owned default list contains the TB Pro and Owl IDs; this patch does not lock either preference or enforce a release-channel policy.",
        "checkInstalledExtensions parses installed extensions concurrently with Promise.allSettled, excludes the two harness add-ons before parsing and retains fulfilled results when resources have already disappeared. The original status preferences count installed entries/Experiments regardless of active state. It passes a Set of add-on-ID:version entries to a dedicated suppression blocklist stash. Equal symmetric difference returns early; changed membership imports only that stash with clear:false and awaits the blocklist update. Native blocklist effects remain a dependency contract, not an executed app-disabled result.",
        "MailGlue runs the scan at startup and on installed/uninstalled/enabled/disabled notifications, then observes changes to the suppression preference. The inspected task does not register an allowed-ID preference observer. Changing the allowed list is reflected when a later scan runs; this source does not establish an immediate scan merely from changing that list.",
        "The permissions observer tests suppression before ordinary update auto-acceptance, sends addon-install-suppressed, rejects the install and returns. A separate failure path substitutes the suppression notification only for incompatible or blocklisted failures; enterprise-policy and signed-state failures retain their distinct handling. The suppression popup is nonpersistent, removes on dismissal, sets a warning icon/name/support URL and removes progress. about:addons returns a warning with encoded ID/name and isSuppressed=true for the alternative search link.",
        "The owned popup markup registers extensionsUI.ftl and uses localized text-link labels. The <> marker remains intentional: options.name is supplied, and the checked comm GlobalPopupNotifications formatter splits the message and reads that name. The original literal Thunderbird wording was not replaced by the requested brand term in this landing despite approval; the inline remains Not Done. Fixed accepted localization uses new -2 IDs, legacy-API wording and the brand term, a later phase.",
        "The five new browser tasks cover a blocked install/no installed add-on, allowlisted permission prompt then cancellation, active temporary install/no warning, off-to-on banner display, and ordinary unsuppressed cancellation. promiseInstallResult removes its listener on every handled terminal event and resolves a reason string; the banner setup intentionally keeps a different listener resolving the actual add-on. The fixture supplies the allowlisted ID and Experiment schema/implementation. The tasks do not directly assert appDisabled or re-enabling after turning suppression off; the banner task summary promises disappearance but only checks off then on. The fixed 500 ms wait remains an explicit lint exception. Current tests later use pushPrefEnv rather than the original direct set/clear calls.",
        "The inherited fixture EventAPI callback/window-listener example is setup evidence, not a new production pattern: its messenger.xul URL and tutorial comments are unchanged example-style setup. All new assertion messages are nonempty and state the expected result with should. Shared checkNotification checks icon, permission-list visibility/count/title and Experiment warning visibility; these static assertions do not establish live keyboard focus, screen-reader output or localized name rendering.",
        "Fixed accepted parseManifest retains the suppression predicate and adds active/special/allowlisted flags. checkInstalledExtensions later filters status preferences using those flags, so its current count semantics are separate from the original. Current about:addons registers an embedder hook after the custom element is defined and forwards expanded/disabled-section context; reuse the existing focused hook lesson instead of reinterpreting the original global wrapper as current code.",
        "Complete primary 2018246 and D284292 timeline, all 21 actual old/resolved/current threads and both literal replacement suggestions were read from original retained records. C3 is the original browser reader; this is Source A retained-context reconciliation, not a second browser confirmation. The early no-tests observation precedes the five owned test tasks; historical green Try/lint claims are not rerun.",
        "Review adoption is checked against the owned source: the allowed-ID list becomes a pref; temporary installs bypass suppression; promiseInstallResult replaces repeated reason-result listeners while the add-on-returning listener stays distinct; the stash compares symmetricDifference rather than adopting the alternative subset-only example. Test splitting after a future pref freeze and locking both prefs are explicitly later plans. The special-treatment/management rationale stays private attributed context; the mozillaAddons explanation was questioned and the author says it is unrelated.",
        "The reviewer asks for wording about Experiment APIs rather than mixing settings with policy, and later asks for the brand term. The owned strings still assert ESR-only support and retain literal Thunderbird in the main message, with the brand inline Not Done; approval is not evidence that those exact wording requests were adopted. Accepted -2 strings and brand terms are later changes. The <> placeholder question is resolved by the actual comm notification formatter and caller name, not by assuming a normal Fluent interpolation.",
        "Added parseManifest JSDoc documents returned fields but uses an object return annotation for an async function; callers correctly await it. This is a scoped documentation observation, not a universal style rule. The tests contain a deliberate fixed-time wait for the negative banner check and do not prove reverse disappearance or native appDisabled state. Accessibility is limited to static localized labels, popup IDs, warning state and support-link wiring."
